One of my big yard projects has been to get rid of the giant gravel driveway and turn it into usable land. Think of a big triangle large enough to park a full size RV on any side, with two points wrapping around the house as a circle driveway and the other point going to the garage. Now picture the middle of the triangle full of 100 years of bricks, concrete, and rock. I've gotten half of the circle around the house gone, and a good third of the triangle.

I finally made my way back to the garage end. The land slopes at a good 1/20 ratio, so water tends to enter the garage during heavy rains. I've decided to build a small swale/hugel bed on the downward slope to catch all the water that goes that way. The soil is pretty much dead right now after probably a good 40 years as a driveway, but it has good texture and composition.

I ordered my trees today, and some of them will go in this area. I will probably cast out a cover crop mix in spring once the whole area is tilled up, then mulch it heavily and let it sit for a year to get some good organisms growing in it.

The whole inside of the triangle will be a fruit orchard eventually, with lots of shade loving shrubs and flowers.
